Server.//: The single most consequential setting. It is announced in EHLO, must match the PTR record for the sending IP, must appear in the TLS certificate SAN list, and is what the MX record points at.

SqlServer.//: In production leave ConnectionString empty and use ConnectionStringSecretName, so no credential is ever written to a JSON file.

Smtp.//: Three listeners, not one with a mode flag. The role is fixed by which socket accepted the connection and is never derived from anything the peer says, so a peer cannot talk its way from port 25 into submission privileges.

InboundMta.//BindAddresses: Empty means every interface. List addresses to narrow it.

Submission.//: Disabled until SASL lands in Milestone 7. A submission listener with no way to authenticate refuses every sender - the correct failure, but not a useful service.

Smtp.//EnableAuthentication: Gates the AUTH capability. False until SASL is implemented and tested; advertising a mechanism the server cannot perform sends clients into a failure they cannot diagnose.
Smtp.//ShutdownGraceSeconds: Abandoning a session mid-DATA risks a duplicate at the sending server, which saw no reply and will retry.
